title: Trinity
definition: The Trinity is the biblical doctrine that there is one true God who eternally exists as three distinct persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Each person is fully God, yet there is one God.
summary: The doctrine of the Trinity guards the biblical truth that God is one, while also honoring the full deity and personal distinction of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Trinity is not three gods, nor one person wearing three roles. Scripture reveals the Father sending the Son, the Son redeeming sinners, and the Holy Spirit applying the work of Christ to believers. This doctrine is central to worship, prayer, salvation, and Christian identity.
christFocus: The Trinity is revealed most clearly through the person and work of Christ. Through the Son we know the Father, and through Christ the Holy Spirit is given to dwell in and empower believers.

studySections.heading: One God
studySections.content: Scripture consistently teaches that there is only one true God. Christian faith is not polytheistic; worship belongs to the one living God alone.

studySections.heading: Three Persons
studySections.content: The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are personally distinct. The Father sends, the Son comes and redeems, and the Spirit proceeds and applies God's saving work.

studySections.heading: Equal Deity
studySections.content: The Son and the Holy Spirit are not created beings. Scripture speaks of them with divine names, works, attributes, and honor.
